definitions.explanation: A school uniform modeled on naval sailor suits, traditionally worn by female middle and high school students in Japan. Features a characteristic sailor collar.

examples.japanese: セーラー{服|ふく}を{着|き}た{女子|じょし}{高生|こうせい}。
examples.english: A high school girl wearing a sailor uniform.

examples.japanese: うちの{中学|ちゅうがく}の{制服|せいふく}はセーラー{服|ふく}だった。
examples.english: My middle school's uniform was a sailor uniform.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}はセーラー{服|ふく}からブレザーに{変|か}える{学校|がっこう}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Recently, more and more schools are switching from sailor uniforms to blazers.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
セーラー{服|ふく} has been a standard school uniform style in Japan since the early 20th century. While historically very common, many schools have been transitioning to ブレザー (blazer) style uniforms. The sailor uniform remains an iconic symbol of Japanese school life.

ETYMOLOGY:
セーラー (sailor) + {服|ふく} (clothing). The design originates from European naval uniforms.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- セーラー{服|ふく}の{学校|がっこう}: a school with sailor uniforms
- {夏服|なつふく}のセーラー{服|ふく}: summer sailor uniform
- {冬服|ふゆふく}のセーラー{服|ふく}: winter sailor uniform
